newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up as investors make long-term plays.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up as investors make long-term plays.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Tuesday as investors bought stocks believed to have solid long-term prospects, such as Telefonica del Peru and UCP Backus, brokers said.
With the market generally buoyant following greater optimism on the New York Stock Exchange, Lima share prices were expected to rise again Wednesday, they added.
Tuesday, the General Index rose 0.15 percent to 1,985.4 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.43 percent to 2,864.9 points, according to preliminary figures.
In a total of 1,799 trades, volume was a modest 28.8 million soles ($10.9 million).

"Local investors were trying to take up positions before an expected inflow of foreign investors," Luis Calderon of local brokerage Acciones y Valores said. Funds from abroad were likely to enter the Lima market because its recent downward trend had made shares cheap, he added.
Tuesday, Peru's top brewer Backus rose 0.88 percent to 2.29 soles on the day's highest volume of 810,000 shares.
Benchmark Telefonica climbed 1.61 percent to 6.30 soles on volume of 764,000 shares.
Tin miner Minsur lost 1.91 percent to close at 8.20 soles on volume of 109,000 shares.
